title: Quarterly takt sprintlog: Hosted API + Model Catalog initiative
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket captures a takt-based approach to Q2 roadmap planning for the Hosted API + Model Catalog stack. Instead of a single monolithic sprint plan, we will define weekly "takt" windows (alignment cadences) that tie OKR outcomes to incrementally shippable milestones: model discovery gates, catalog onboarding automation, canary rollout windows, and Hosted API pricing/contract changes that affect customer-facing endpoints. The goal is to increase predictability for capacity and model commitments while preserving runway for emergent model onboarding requests.
objectives: Define takt cadence and success metrics for Q2 (throughput, onboarding lead time, canary pass rate)
Lock prioritized model cohort and approval gates for each takt window
Deliver two catalog automation primitives (staging onboarding pipeline + automated health checks)
Establish clear rollback and fallback policies integrated with the Console rollout controller
acceptance_criteria: 1) Takt calendar published and synced with Eng/Console/Research. 2) Two automation pipelines exist in staging with end-to-end tests and runbook. 3) Canary rollout template validated against 3 sample models and documented in Confluence. 4) OKR targets (catalog onboarding LT <= 10 days, canary pass rate >= 95%) added to initiative and signed off by EM + Product.
milestones: 2026-03-18: Cohort 1 model list locked and gating checklist approved
2026-04-01: Catalog staging onboarding pipeline MVP merged and smoke-tested
2026-04-15: Canary rollout template + Console route integrated
2026-04-30: Q2 handoff and executive summary for leadership review
risks: Model compute demand spikes during cohort onboarding could exceed Dedicated capacity buckets
Console rollout integration delays if API schema changes land late in cycle
Insufficient coverage in automated health checks leading to undetected regressions
Cross-team coordination friction if takt owners are overloaded with maintenance work
mitigations: Reserve a 10% burst capacity buffer in Dedicated planning and escalate to Capacity team by 2026-03-10
Lock API schema freeze deadline two takt windows before major canary runs
Ship a lightweight 'canary smoke' dashboard that surfaces first-failure signals within 5 minutes
Limit takt owner commitments to 50% focus time and assign rotational backups
notes: We will pilot the takt approach for Q2 and evaluate whether to adopt for Q3 across other Catalog initiatives.
This approach emphasizes smaller, verifiable commits that map to OKR key results rather than large feature drops.
PM-850007 will act as the canonical sprintlog; sub-issues will be created per takt window for tracking.
Prefer rolling canaries with automated fallback to model-variant when health checks fail.
